About the Department
Welcome to the Department of Geography at Moran Mahila Mahavidyalaya. As one of the newest departments of the college, we are committed to academic excellence and holistic development, striving to build a strong educational foundation while keeping pace with modern advancements in geographical studies.
The Department of Geography at Moran Mahila Mahavidyalaya was established in 2025 under the Faculty of Earth Sciences, affiliated with Dibrugarh University. It began its academic journey with an initial batch of 10 students in the major course and 12 students in the minor course at the undergraduate level. Since its inception, the department has aimed to provide quality education that bridges traditional learning with modern applications, in accordance with the curriculum prescribed by Dibrugarh University.
Beyond academics, we are committed to nurturing socially responsible and environmentally conscious individuals, ensuring that students achieve academic success and make positive contributions to their communities, society, and the earth.
About the course:
The three-year undergraduate program encompasses both physical geography, covering landforms, climate, soils, and the environment, as well as human geography, which includes population, settlement, economic activities, urban studies, and political geography. Students also gain hands-on exposure to advanced tools such as Geographic Information Systems (GIS), remote sensing, and cartography.
The department's well-equipped laboratory fosters hands-on learning, reinforcing theoretical knowledge through fieldwork and technical applications.
Vision:
To emerge as one of the leading centres for geographical education and research for women in the upper Assam region of Assam, India, through spatial understanding of people–environment relationships, sustainable development, and regional growth.
Mission:
The Department promotes interdisciplinary and applied learning through GIS, remote sensing, cartography, and spatial analysis while fostering critical thinking, analytical skills, and effective communication for informed decision-making. It encourages research and innovation to address environmental, migration, and development challenges, with a focus on real-world applications. The Department also aims to enhance employability and leadership, contributing to sustainable regional development through community engagement and field-based learning.
About the discipline:
Geography is a multifaceted discipline that examines the interactions between the natural and human worlds, as well as the spatial patterns and processes that shape our planet. Encompassing diverse subfields such as physical geography, human geography, environmental geography, and geospatial sciences, it integrates perspectives from both the natural and social sciences. Through the study of geography, students gain a deeper understanding of the complex relationships between society, space, and the environment, while also developing the knowledge and skills to address pressing issues of sustainability, resource management, and spatial development.
At the Honours level, the curriculum encourages analytical and spatial thinking and prepares students for advanced study and research. Graduates in geography can pursue postgraduate programmes or opt for specialised diploma courses in areas such as Geographical Information Systems (GIS), cartography, remote sensing, and population studies.
Employment opportunities are available not only in the field of education but also in various government and research organisations such as the Census of India, National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO), Survey of India, Town and Country Planning Departments, Disaster Management Authorities, and environmental consultancies.
Furthermore, geography is one of the most widely chosen and scoring subjects in national and state-level civil service examinations, making it a preferred choice for students aspiring for careers in administrative services. The subject, thus, provides a balanced foundation for academic, technical, and administrative careers.
Prospects:
The department aims to become a center of excellence in teaching, research, and community engagement. In the coming years, it plans to:
Introduce certificate courses in GIS, remote sensing, and disaster management to enhance students’ employability.
Develop modern laboratory and field-based facilities for practical learning.
Promote research on regional issues, such as climate change, migration, and sustainable development.
Build collaborations with academic and government institutions like Assam Science Technology and Environment Council (ASTEC), North Eastern Space Applications Centre (NESAC), and Assam State Disaster Management Authority for knowledge exchange.
Conduct workshops, awareness programmes, and local surveys on environmental management, disaster preparedness, and rural development to connect classroom learning with real-world applications.
